concepts.name: Type assertions do not validate runtime data

questions.prompt: A parsed API payload is asserted with `as User`. Which runtime guarantee does that assertion add?

choices.text: A conversion that fills every required User property with a default value.
A prototype change that makes the parsed object an instance of User.
None; an explicit runtime check is still needed to establish its shape.
A recursive property check that throws when the payload misses a field.

questions.explanation: Type assertions are removed and do not validate or transform runtime data. External data needs explicit checks before trusting its shape.

sources.title: TypeScript: Everyday Types
sources.claim: Type assertions are erased and perform no runtime checks; any disables checks while union members require narrowing.

questions.prompt: A union contains object values and null. Why is `typeof value === "object"` alone insufficient before reading a field?

choices.text: Every object value becomes a string after its typeof result is compared.
JavaScript also reports object for null, so a null check is needed.
TypeScript treats every object branch as any and forbids further narrowing.
The typeof operation validates every field but never allows property access.

questions.explanation: TypeScript accounts for the JavaScript typeof null behavior. A separate null exclusion is needed to safely access object fields.

sources.title: TypeScript: Narrowing
sources.claim: TypeScript narrows unions through control flow, discriminants and predicates; never supports exhaustive checks.

questions.prompt: A result union uses `kind: "ok"` with data and `kind: "error"` with message. What helps select the right member?

choices.text: Check kind before accessing the fields specific to that variant.
Assert the union as the ok member without testing the discriminant.
Read both variant fields directly because a union contains their intersection.
Make kind a general string so any comparison narrows to every member.

questions.explanation: A shared literal discriminant narrows a union to the appropriate member. Unions do not permit unchecked access to members that only some variants contain.

questions.prompt: A switch handles every member of a discriminated union and assigns the default branch value to never. Why is that useful?

choices.text: The assignment ensures every runtime payload is automatically validated.
The assignment causes TypeScript to emit a switch case for each missing member.
The assignment deletes unknown variants from network response objects.
A newly added unhandled variant makes the never assignment fail type checking.

questions.explanation: Never represents the absence of remaining variants after exhaustive narrowing. An unhandled new member is not assignable to never, but this does not validate external runtime data.

questions.prompt: An API parser exposes its unvalidated result as unknown rather than any. What changes at the call site?

choices.text: The runtime automatically checks unknown properties before every read.
The emitted JavaScript stores unknown values in a different object format.
The caller must narrow or assert the value before using its specific properties.
The caller can access every property because unknown disables checking.

questions.explanation: Unknown requires establishing a type before specific use. Any instead allows unchecked operations; neither type changes the runtime object format.

sources.title: TypeScript: More on Functions
sources.claim: unknown permits arbitrary values but does not permit property use without narrowing; unlike any, it retains checking at unvalidated boundaries.

questions.prompt: A value is string or number. A branch checks `typeof value === "string"`. What can TypeScript infer inside that branch?

choices.text: The value becomes any because primitive tests erase all type information.
The value is a string and string-specific operations are available.
The value remains the full union because typeof never affects static types.
The value becomes a string at runtime even if it originally was a number.

questions.explanation: TypeScript recognizes typeof guards and narrows the branch. The check tests the actual value; it does not perform conversion.

questions.prompt: A service accepts JSON from outside its process. Which boundary claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A non-null assertion proves a server never returns null.
A declared interface automatically validates incoming JSON.
An assertion does not check the payload at runtime.
Explicit shape checks can establish runtime facts.
as User fills missing fields in the payload.

questions.explanation: a: The assertion is not evidence or a runtime check. b: A static declaration does not run a parser or validator. c: Assertions are erased without runtime validation. d: The application must implement those checks for untrusted values. e: It does not transform the runtime object.

questions.prompt: A function narrows a union with runtime checks. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: typeof object proves every expected property exists.
typeof guards can narrow primitive unions.
A null check matters when testing object values.
Control flow can affect the type at each branch.
A typeof comparison coerces the value into that type.

questions.explanation: a: That broad test does not validate the object shape. b: TypeScript recognizes the checked primitive types. c: typeof null is object. d: Reachability and checks drive narrowing. e: It tests rather than converts the value.

questions.prompt: A discriminated union models success and failure. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A common literal-valued field can identify a member.
Checking the discriminant permits variant-specific access.
Every union property is present on every runtime variant.
A general string field always identifies exactly one member.
An assertion replaces the need to test an external variant.

questions.explanation: a: That field provides the discriminant. b: The selected branch is narrowed to matching members. c: Members may have different fields. d: Distinct literal values provide the precise discrimination. e: An assertion does not establish which variant actually arrived.

questions.prompt: A switch uses a never check in its default branch. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A new unhandled union member can cause a compile error.
The pattern supports maintenance as the union grows.
It validates every external runtime value automatically.
It generates missing case implementations at runtime.
Fully handled variants leave no remaining member there.

questions.explanation: a: That member is not assignable to never. b: It exposes missing handling during type checking. c: Static exhaustiveness assumes the declared type is accurate. d: Type checking does not write those application branches. e: Exhaustive narrowing yields never.
